Blocks.Text: As a LinkedIn partner, you must sync your customers' access control lists (ACLs) so that their data is visible to the appropriate users in LinkedIn. Module 4 covers linking job requisitions to security groups or roles, assigning users to those groups, and verifying visibility in One Click Export and the In-ATS Indicator. To complete Module 4 certification, demonstrate each applicable test case below to LinkedIn.
Test cases are grouped by the aspect of ACL sync being exercised.

Test cases in this module use the functional, qualitative, and charter check types. For the rule ID scheme, how to read each test case, and the check type definitions, refer to the certification overview.

The table below maps each test case's previous Rule ID (used in earlier revisions of
this document) to its new Rule ID.

Map entity ACL and assignee data models (certification prerequisite)1. Produce a field-level mapping of your ATS security-group or role → the LinkedIn entityAcl schema (entityAclId, entityId, entityType = JOB_REQUISITION, dataProvider = ATS, integrationContext, externalCreatedAt, externalLastModifiedAt).2. Map your user-membership model → the entityAclAssignee schema (entityAclId, assignee = person URN, dataProvider = ATS, integrationContext, externalCreatedAt, externalLastModifiedAt).3. State how you resolve each user to a person URN (refer to Bind Customer Users).

• Review the mapping between your ATS security-group or role and user-membership models and the LinkedIn entityAcl and entityAclAssignee schemas.• This mapping is a certification prerequisite used for the LinkedIn testing and verification (code review).Related documentation: ACL overview

Verify ACL and assignee ID fidelity1. Show entityAclId equals your security-group or role id (strict 1:1).2. Show entityId equals your externalJobRequisitionId (the same IDs synced in Module 2) and entityType uses the correct Securable Entity Type enum (JOB_REQUISITION).3. Show assignee equals the user's bound person URN.4. No fabricated IDs; no added prefix or suffix.5. Share the code block or API signature or sample payload where these IDs are sourced.

• entityAclId, entityId (= externalJobRequisitionId), and assignee (person URN) must each be identical to your own source IDs (strict one-to-one).• Fabricated or generated IDs are not allowed, and no added prefix or suffix is permitted.• Verification (code review): share a code block or API signature or sample API payload showing where these IDs are sourced, so LinkedIn can confirm the mapping — analogous to the Module 2 Entity ID Fidelity deliverables.

Add an ACL assignee and verify access to a secured job requisition1. Create two new job requisitions with accessRestricted = true through PUT rest/jobRequisitions, for example, jobReq-1 and jobReq-2.2. Create the ACL group (for example, User1_ACL) securing both job requisitions (jobReq-1, jobReq-2) through PUT rest/entityAcls.3. Assign the user (User1, through person URN) to the ACL group (User1_ACL) through PUT rest/entityAclAssignees.4. Visit User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter and show, from the One-Click Export dropdown, that both job requisitions (jobReq-1, jobReq-2) are visible.5. To list the ACL groups a user belongs to, call GET rest/entityAclAssignees.

• All PUT and GET API calls succeed (verify from logs or response status).• On User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter, both job requisitions (jobReq-1, jobReq-2) are visible in the One-Click Export dropdown.

Verify ACL assignee access to an atsApplication for a secured job requisition1. Create one new job requisition with accessRestricted = true through PUT rest/jobRequisitions, for example, jobReq-1.2. Create the ACL group (for example, User1_ACL) securing this job requisition (jobReq-1) through PUT rest/entityAcls.3. Assign the Recruiter user (User1, through person URN) to the ACL group (User1_ACL) through PUT rest/entityAclAssignees.4. Create a new atsApplication for this candidate and job requisition combination through PUT rest/applications.5. Visit User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter and show that the created atsApplication is visible in the In-ATS Indicator or under the ATS tab → Jobs and Feedback section.

• All PUT and GET API calls succeed (verify from logs or response status).• On User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter, the application to the job requisition is visible in the In-ATS Indicator and under the ATS tab → Jobs and Feedback section.

Remove a job requisition from a secured view for a user1. Create two new job requisitions with accessRestricted = true through PUT rest/jobRequisitions, for example, jobReq-1 and jobReq-2.2. Create the ACL group (for example, User1_ACL) securing both job requisitions (jobReq-1, jobReq-2) through PUT rest/entityAcls.3. Assign the user (User1, through person URN) to the ACL group (User1_ACL) through PUT rest/entityAclAssignees.4. Visit User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter and show, from the One-Click Export dropdown, that both job requisitions (jobReq-1, jobReq-2) are visible.5. Remove one of the job requisitions (for example, jobReq-1) from the user's ACL group through DELETE rest/entityAcls.6. Visit User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter again and confirm, from the One-Click Export dropdown, that jobReq-1 is no longer visible while jobReq-2 still is.

• All PUT, GET, and DELETE API calls succeed (verify from logs or response status).• On User1's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter, exactly one of the two job requisitions remains visible in the One-Click Export dropdown — jobReq-2 is visible and jobReq-1 is not.

Create and manage generic ACL groups1. Create a job requisition (for example, jobReq-1) with accessRestricted = true.2. Create an ACL group (for example, MANAGER) associated with the job requisition (jobReq-1) through PUT rest/entityAcls.3. Add a Recruiter user (for example, User1) to the same ACL group through PUT rest/entityAclAssignees.4. Visit User1's LinkedIn profile within LinkedIn Recruiter and confirm the One-Click Export dropdown shows the secured job requisition (jobReq-1).5. Visit any other user's LinkedIn profile within Recruiter and confirm the One-Click Export dropdown does not show the secured job requisition (jobReq-1).6. Add another user (for example, User2) to the same ACL group (MANAGER) and confirm User2 can also view jobReq-1 from the One-Click Export dropdown.7. Add another secured job requisition (for example, jobReq-2, accessRestricted = true) to the same ACL group (MANAGER) and confirm User2 can also view the newly added job requisition (jobReq-2).

• All PUT and GET API calls succeed (verify from logs or response status).• Every user assigned to the MANAGER ACL group (User1, User2) sees the group's secured job requisitions in the One-Click Export dropdown.• Any user not assigned to the MANAGER ACL group does not see the group's secured job requisitions.• Adding a user to the group grants that user visibility of every job requisition already in the group, and adding a job requisition to the group makes it visible to every user already in the group — confirming group membership governs visibility for both users and job requisitions.

Update generic ACL group membership1. Continued from RSC-401-006.2. Remove a job requisition (for example, jobReq-1, accessRestricted = true) from the ACL group (for example, MANAGER).3. Visit the user's LinkedIn profile within LinkedIn Recruiter and confirm the One-Click Export dropdown no longer shows the secured job requisition (jobReq-1).4. Remove a user (for example, User2) from the ACL group (MANAGER).5. Confirm the removed user (User2) can no longer view the secured job requisitions in the One-Click Export dropdown that were visible earlier.

• All PUT, GET, and DELETE API calls succeed (verify from logs or response status).• After jobReq-1 is removed from the MANAGER group, assigned users no longer see jobReq-1 in the One-Click Export dropdown, while job requisitions still in the group (for example, jobReq-2) remain visible.• After User2 is removed from the MANAGER group, User2 no longer sees any of the group's secured job requisitions in the One-Click Export dropdown, while users still in the group retain visibility.

Re-add an ACL assignee1. Re-add the user(s) to the ACL or security group: PUT rest/entityAclAssignees with the user's person URN.2. Log in as one of the re-added users and check the One-Click Export dropdown and the In-ATS Indicator for any candidate.
• Logged in as one of the re-added users, they are able to see the secured job requisitions again in the One-Click Export dropdown and in the In-ATS Indicator for any candidate.

Blocks.Text: These test cases apply across all ACL sync in Module 4.

Rows.Text: Verify idempotent ACL and assignee upserts1. Re-send an already-synced entityAcl (same entityAclId, entityId, entityType, and integrationContext) and an already-synced entityAclAssignee (same entityAclId, assignee, and integrationContext), keeping the complete key unchanged.2. Show the batch calls are grouped in ≤ 100 records in sequential order.

• LinkedIn upserts the existing ACL or assignee — it must not create a second copy.• This complements the Entity ID Fidelity rule (RSC-401-002): stable, one-to-one IDs are what make idempotent upserts possible.

Keep ACLs current on change1. Add or update a user or a job requisition and show the corresponding entityAcl or entityAclAssignee is re-synced to prevent visibility issues.2. Confirm you do not assign more than 10 ACLs per user.3. Confirm batches are grouped in ≤ 100 records per call, with multiple batches for larger volumes.

• ACLs and assignees are updated when users or job requisitions are added or updated, so visibility stays correct.• No more than 10 ACLs are assigned per user, and batch calls respect the 100-record limit.

Verify ACL coverage of securable entitiesUse the loaded customer test tenant.1. Produce the ACL coverage report and confirm the threshold is met.2. The LinkedIn team will share the data quality report for the records present in LinkedIn.
Ensure the data quality requirement is met:• < 5% of securable entities (for example, job requisitions) are without ACLs

Re-run ACL checks during the charter phase1. Once the functional and data quality checks pass, re-run the same ACL functional and qualitative checks on the charter customer tenant(s).2. Obtain sign-off from the product managers and the RSC or CRM Connect team.3. This is a LinkedIn internal checklist item.

Once the functional and qualitative checks pass, you are ready for beta. Re-run the same ACL functional and qualitative checks on the charter customer tenant(s). Charter-phase metrics must be reviewed and signed off by the product managers and the RSC or CRM Connect team before certification (GA).
